verdict.rationale: AWS documents the core mechanism for exactly this story: IAM roles/STS assume-role issue temporary session credentials with no long-term keys (aws-docs-12, aws-docs-46), permissions boundaries and identity/resource policies can narrowly scope what a role can do (aws-docs-11, aws-docs-28), and OIDC/IdP federation extends this to external non-human callers (aws-docs-13, aws-docs-29, aws-docs-47). AWS also explicitly targets AI agents with Bedrock AgentCore, which 'helps you handle the authentication and access control' when an agent must call multiple tools/APIs in a turn, built on this same security model (aws-docs-24, aws-docs-35, aws-docs-45). Missing for 10: an explicit, agent-specific worked example showing least-privilege session-policy scoping/escalation prevention end-to-end, and independent/hands-on corroboration beyond AWS's own docs.
